introduction: Obligation of Islamic Will and Testament; From Quran and Sunnah
In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful

"It is prescribed for you that when any of you approaches death, if he leaves any good, let him make a will for the parents and other relatives. This is a duty for those who are mindful of God." (2:180).
Narrated by Abdullah bin 'Umar, radi Allah Anhu: Allah's Messenger, salla Allah Alayhi wa sallam, said,
"It is not permissible for any Muslim who has something to will, to stay for two nights without having his last will and testament written and kept ready with him. "

The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) has emphasized the preparation of a Will at one's earliest opportunity. According to a narration reported by Abdullah ibn Umar (ra), the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: “It is not befitting for a Muslim who has something to make a Will of, to remain for two nights without having one’s last Will and testament written and kept ready with one.” (Sahih Bukhari)

3. Executors or Administrators of the estate may be relatives who stand to inherit from the testator, or any other reliable and trustworthy Muslims.

not stand to inherit, should be selected.
5. An inventory must be made of all movable and immovable assets and all property belonging to the estate, upon demise. The testator should mention in Addendum A, details of any property or
belongings of which only he/she has knowledge.
6. A minor may not be a witness to the Will.
